rationale: PINS the OTHER side of the primitive filter, which `type-usage-graph` pins for container builtins (dict/list). The analyzer's rule is: of the names written in a TYPE POSITION, only the 11 scalars (`str int float complex bool bytes object None Any self cls`) are dropped — every other name is the type the code NAMES, and an interpreter builtin is not an exception to that. This fixture fixes the boundary at the exception hierarchy and at `type`, which `python-endpoint-defects.ts` class D2 counted as unspecified: `slot: Exception` (annotation), `isinstance(stream, Exception)` (runtime check), `-> BaseException | None` (annotation + union) and `-> type` all emit `references`; the scalars `None` (in the union and the return) stay filtered. `builtin-type-name-is-not-a-control-flow-edge` pins the other direction — an `except Exception` clause is NOT a type position and emits nothing — so the two fixtures together say where the edge comes from instead of only that it exists.
